text: Friday, four in the morning. Out at sea, Kanghan's barge is lit up like a stadium.
Geum has a new order. Today you stop carrying. The lid breaks in two days and she wants him to stop? She wants him to learn to hold.
She tells Borro to hit her, in field form, with everything he has. All of it?
He slams his iron shield into her ladle. The concrete cracks under her slippers. She doesn't move.
And the force doesn't go anywhere. It stays in the ladle, humming.
Then she turns and taps a tetrapod the size of a car, and it splits clean in two.
Pim is beside himself. She broke a rock with a spoon.
A wall doesn't push back, Geum says. It holds. Then it gives it back.
That was her S-rank skill, holding the hit. Was, she says. Her steel arm still remembers it.
She didn't pass it on. She kept it, and then she chose where it went.
So Jaeha does what he always does. He reads the fine print of his own skill. Pass, clause three: force in transit may be held by the Operator. Risk, bone damage.
Nobody ever reads clause three.
First try. Geum strikes Borro's shield, and Jaeha catches the force through the link instead of passing it on.
He can't hold it. It bursts out through his hand into the concrete, and his finger bends the wrong way.
Again in four hours, Geum says. That's his cooldown, isn't it?
She splints the finger with a chopstick. It's only cracked. He has nine more.
At six, out at sea, the barge starts to drill.
Pim winces at every boom. They've started. And it hates it.
Jaeha writes the day out left-handed. Borro's field form comes back every four hours. Four tries.
Eight o'clock. Second try. This time the glow stays in his chest.
Hold it, Geum says. Like the cup. Don't spill a drop.
New skill: Store. One strike, held for three seconds.
Then he lays his hand on Borro's shield and gives the force back. Like a wall.
At noon he holds it for ten seconds, his whole arm glowing, his bones creaking.
And the count is falling faster. Forty hours left, because of the drilling.
Someone should go and look at what they're doing to it, Lyra says. His link only reaches six hundred metres. Then get a boat. She's river-folk.
So at one-thirty, a little fishing boat chugs out toward the barge, riding very low with Borro aboard.
It belongs to the old fisherman Jaeha saved on Tuesday night. The boat is his all day.
Kanghan's troopers order them to turn back. Han Sora waves from the rail. Fishing, Mr. Kang?
Lyra climbs onto the side of the boat in field form and a swimsuit. Try not to look, merchant.
She dives straight down.
Pim opens his wings and guides her down with his voice. Thirty metres down, then swim for the barge. The lid is under them.
Through the link, Jaeha sees the lid: a disc of stone and steel too big to see the edge of, and Kanghan's new anchor bolts drilled into it.
And a crack spreading out from the drill holes, with violet light seeping through.
They aren't reinforcing the lid. They're breaking it.
Below the crack, a violet glow hangs like a lantern, and something vast turns past it. Lyra's hand drifts toward the light. Pim screams at her to listen to his voice.
Forty seconds of field form left.
She bursts out of the sea onto the barge's fender, right under Sora, and blows her a kiss. Your bolts are crooked, darling.
Sora just smiles. She's good.
The old fisherman brings the boat in under the barge to fetch her. The smile is gone. Something down there looked at her, and she wanted to go to it. Jaeha saw it too.
At four, Moon Ahin calls her uncle. Stop the drilling. You're cracking the lid.
Do you want Busan dark, Ahin?
She hangs up on him.
On the breakwater, Jaeha holds Borro's blocked hit for thirty seconds, glowing from his chest to his fingertips.
Five percent left on the lid. Thirty hours.
At six-forty, a girl with a school backpack walks up the harbour road.
It's Seoa. It's Friday, and dinner is at seven. He promised. The budget has a train ticket in it now.
Geum and Seoa size each other up. So you're the budget. And you're the one feeding my brother for free.
Then they bow to each other at the exact same moment. Sit, you're eating. Thank you, I'll do the dishes.
The two of them agree on everything. Jaeha is doomed.
Seoa finds the chopstick taped to his finger. Training, he says.
Six fifty-eight. Everyone is round the counter, bowls out, the bulbs warm. They eat at seven.
The clock ticks to six fifty-nine.
Out on the barge, an engineer punches the air. They're through.
And violet light bursts up out of the seabed under the barge.
Pim drops his chopsticks. It's awake.
The lid drops to one percent. Estimated failure: fifty-nine minutes.
Geum's steel fist clenches on its own, and she picks up her ladle.
Around the counter, everyone has turned toward the sea. Seoa grips her brother's sleeve.
Geum stands. Kid. Dinner's late.
